newsitem.title: USA: US spot fuel oil prices steady despite lower crude.
newsitem.headline: US spot fuel oil prices steady despite lower crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices held steady in thin activity Friday on continued strong interest in high sulphur material in the U.S. Gulf despite sharply lower crude prices.
"The market was very quiet today," said a Houston trader.
In addition to relatively tight spot supply of HSFO in the Gulf, there were concerns over transportation problems along Mississippi River after a barge accident restricted traffic flow since Monday.
"At this point, most of the barges could go in one direction, down river," said one Houston cash dealer.
Limited ability to transport resid materials from refiners along the Gulf is expected to aggravate the perceived supply tightness of HSFO, market sources said.
Overall resid demand remained light due to cheap natural gas for industrial consumption and inexpensive spot electricity supplies available to utilities, traders noted.
NYH one percent physical held at $16.00-25 a barrel, while one percent NYH paper for April remained at $15.90-16.10.
NYMEX May crude contract settled down 34 cents at $21.51 a bbl after posting a high at $22.22.
NYH HSFO was steady with three percent at $13.25-75. The 0.3 percent high pour grade stayed near $17.00.
In the U.S. Gulf, three percent sulphur grade stablized after this week's gains at $14.25-75. Three percent paper was notionally assessed at $13.90-14.25, flat from Thursday.
USG one percent physical strengthened toward $15.00 from yesterday's $14.75 a barrel.

At the New York City gate, day-ahead natural gas continued to falter, down to $2.18-2.22 per million British thermal units or $13.86 a barrel equivalent from Thursday's $2.21-2.28/mmBtu and $14.18/bbl equivalent.
Natgas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, remained near $1.87/mmBtu or 11.78/bbl equivalent.
